elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: §3.4 as rendered: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month". Service Option Attachments are the Order-Form-referenced attachments, so both Agreement-level and order-level convenience exits exist. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present = false" is a false negative caused by the interposed parenthetical between "terminate" and "for convenience"; the operative right is plainly present.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice is "at least one month's prior written notice" and termination can only take effect "at the end of any calendar month", so the effective date can fall materially more than 30 days after notice. To meet the preferred element the drafter would have to state termination effective 30 days after written notice, untethered from calendar month end.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic anywhere in the rendered §§3.2–3.4; §3.4(b) only requires Customer to pay early termination charges. A pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period would have to be inserted.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only mid-term exit is §3.3 material-breach termination; its only unilateral exit is the §3.2 non-renewal notice given 90 days before term end, which is a RENEWAL mechanic, not a mid-term convenience right. No Vendor convenience termination exists during the committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: §3.4 gives Customer a convenience right on "at least one month's prior written notice" effective at calendar month end — shorter and more favourable than the 60–90 day fallback ceiling, so the fallback threshold is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Edited §3.4(b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three months' recurring charges for terminated Services." The cap is stated in operative text and its basis (recurring charges for the terminated Services) cannot exceed three months of fees, so the ceiling is no higher than the checklist permits.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not bite: IBM has no convenience termination right at all. §3.3 is breach-only (mutual) and §3.2 is an auto-renewal/non-renewal notice evaluated under RENEWAL. A vendor with no convenience right satisfies "only at the end of a term".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply because IBM has no convenience termination right; separately, the only IBM-initiated exit (§3.2 non-renewal) requires written notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: Customer's one-month convenience right (better than 60–90 days), the newly inserted three-month cap on early termination charges, and the absence of any Vendor convenience right (breach-only under §3.3; §3.2 is non-renewal) cover all four fallback elements.

Preferred level is not complete: no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, and the calendar-month-end anchor means the effective date can exceed 30 days from notice. Both are correctly flagged as preferred-only gaps rather than redlined.
Deviation classification is sound: before the edit the clause failed the fallback on a material term because the Attachment A early termination charges were open-ended and unbounded.

Minimality holds: a single clause-tail insertion in §3.4(b), the earlier cosmetic relocation of "for convenience" reverted, no survival tails, no added procedures, and no deletion of favourable existing language (including the §3.3 proviso barring IBM from recovering early termination charges after its own breach).

Intent preserved: the Attachment A / Service Option Attachment cross-references survive, the §3.3 reference to "the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b)" remains coherent, and no undefined term or contradictory retained sentence is created.

Drafting note (non-blocking): "three months' recurring charges for terminated Services" uses a narrower basis than "fees"; it is Customer-favourable, but if Attachment A imposes one-time exit charges the drafter may wish to confirm the cap reaches all early termination charges, not just recurring-charge-based ones.
